transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

I'm here because I'm having a really hard time with how I look, especially at work. I teach high school, and... well, I just can’t stop seeing this crooked, swollen-looking side of my face whenever I have to look at the lesson videos we record. It's really getting to me. 

Once I see it, I can't focus on anything else. I just feel like the students, their parents, the other staff... I feel like they must all be staring right at it instead of actually listening to anything I’m saying.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time thinking about this part of your face, maybe checking it in mirrors, covering it up, or trying to fix it in some way?

Yeah, I do. A lot. Especially with the video stuff for school. 

Before I post a recorded lesson or... or join a video conference with parents, I just keep changing the camera angle, trying to find a way where it doesn't look so obvious. I'll replay the clips over and over, and a lot of the time I end up just kind of resting my hand on that side of my face while I talk to try and cover it up. 

I've actually been re-recording whole lessons so many times that I completely miss my prep work for the day. It's getting really bad because I'm ending up falling behind and being late with my actual classes, just trying to get a video where my face doesn't look so messed up.
Do you think others notice or comment on this issue with your face, or do you feel like it's something that only you can really see?

Honestly, no one has actually... said anything to me about it. No one's made a comment or pointed it out. 

But I still feel like they have to be noticing it. It's just so obvious to me when I look at the screen, so I assume they see it too and are maybe just... I don't know, being polite by not bringing it up. But yeah, to answer your question, no one has actually said anything to me directly.
Have you ever used any substances, like stimulants or hallucinogens, either recreationally or for any other reason?
No, I don't use anything like that. I don't do drugs or take any kind of stimulants or hallucinogens. I just stick to coffee, really.
Has this concern about your appearance affected any other parts of your life, like your relationships, sleep, or ability to enjoy activities you used to like?

Yeah, it really has. Mostly with work and the activities I do at the school. Like I mentioned earlier about the videos taking up so much time, I've fallen way behind on my regular lesson planning. And it's bleeding into other things, too. 

I do some student mentoring, and I coach the basketball team, but... I just can't get my actual work finished on time anymore, so I'm dropping the ball there as well. It's gotten pretty bad. The administrators have actually started documenting my missed deadlines and the issues I've been having with class coverage. I'm... I'm honestly worried that I'm close to losing my position over all this.
Can you describe what you see on that side of your face that concerns you so much, and how does it compare to how others have described your appearance?

It's... it's just this one side of my face. When I'm recording those lesson videos, I look at the screen and it just looks completely crooked. And swollen, too. Like one side is just drooping and puffy compared to the other. 

Once I notice it on the screen, I just can't stop seeing it. And then I start thinking about how the students are watching these videos, and the parents, and the other staff... and I just feel like they must be staring right at it. Like they aren't even listening to the lesson or anything I'm saying because they're too busy looking at how messed up my face is. But like I said before, no one has actually described it to me or said anything about it. It's just what I see.
